title: Introduce subtle-flat variant + deterministic loading cancellation for clustered icon buttons
creator: Ava Chen
description: Problem: Multiple product teams want a low-contrast, flush button style for dense toolbars (esp. in embedded UIs) that feels tappable but does not introduce additional elevation or heavy outlines. Current 'ghost' and 'compact' variants either look too weak or rely on elevation tokens that break in high-contrast themes. Secondary problem: clustered icon buttons (icon groups with adjacent action buttons) show inconsistent loading behavior — spinners shift layout, cancellation is ambiguous, and keyboard users lose context when focus jumps.
acceptance_criteria: Design a new 'subtle-flat' variant that is visually distinct from 'ghost' and 'primary' and maps to a stable token set that degrades gracefully across themes (light/dark/high-contrast)
Define token mappings (background, border, icon-tint, hover/focus states, disabled) and list which existing tokens to reuse vs new tokens to add

Behaviour: clustered-icon buttons must support a deterministic 'load/cancel' contract where an action can be in-progress without shifting layout and a cancel control is exposed to both mouse and keyboard users

Accessibility: keyboard focus order is preserved when a loading state is entered; screen-readers announce loading + cancel affordance; motion-reduction respects spinner suppression and shows static progress indicator fallback
Engineering: implement CSS token references and a small JS helper to coordinate deterministic cancellation and focus retention; include unit & visual regression tests
Rollout: feature flags for 2 weeks behind a console toggle, metrics dashboard to look for regressions in click rates and keyboard flow failures
design_notes: 'Subtle-flat' should have 0 elevation, 1px inset border token only for light themes, and an elevated-like tactile hover (color shift) rather than shadow to avoid layout shifts in constrained toolbars
Color strategy: base-bg uses --token-surface-0, hover uses --token-surface-0-emphasized (new token), icon tint uses --token-icon-secondary; disabled uses --token-surface-muted and --token-icon-muted
Motion: spinner only appears if prefers-reduced-motion == false and if the action takes > 200ms. Otherwise show a small pulsing ringless indicator (static dot) for reduced-motion users
Edge-case: when grouped with a primary CTA, subtle-flat must not steal affordance. Add 'context-aware' borderless rule: adjacent-to-primary reduces contrast slightly
Token migration: provide migration table from legacy ghost/compact tokens to new subtle-flat tokens in the PR description
engineering_tasks: Create new token entries in tokens.json and map to CSS variables (tokens: surface.subtle-flat-bg, surface.subtle-flat-hover, icon.subtle-flat)
Add Button variant 'subtle-flat' to component library with props: size, loading, cancelableLoading, iconOnlyClusterBehavior
Implement deterministic loading controller: when loading=true and cancelableLoading=true, keep button size constant and append an ARIA-visible cancel button; ensure focus trap is avoided
Add keyboard behavior: Esc cancels loading if cancelable; Tab order keeps cancel button after primary action; preserve last-focused control on cancel
Write visual regression tests (Chromatic/Playwright snapshots) across themes and densities
Add unit tests for token fallbacks and accessibility announcements (Jest + a11y runner)
Add telemetry hooks to track instances of clustered icon loading and cancel usage (event names: btn.loading.started, btn.loading.cancelled)
Run a 48-hour canary behind console toggle and collect regressions: click-through, keyboard abandonment, visual diffs
review_comments: 2026-01-12 - Priya Singh (PM): Love the low-contrast direction. Please confirm that the subtle-flat won't become the de-facto default for form actions — we should gate adoption via component docs and code examples.

2026-01-15 - Marcus Ortiz (Engineering): Implementation sounds fine; we should avoid adding a runtime dependency for cancel behavior — prefer a small in-component controller that accepts a CancellationToken from calling code.

2026-01-18 - Ben Morales (Accessibility): Ensure screen reader message format: 'Saving, press Esc to cancel' and ARIA-live polite region updates. Also confirm that cancel control is reachable by keyboard without requiring extra tab stops for most flows.
2026-01-22 - Elena Rios (Design): Updated figma with micro-variants for 24/20/16px sizes, included high-contrast mockups. See attachment.

2026-01-28 - Luca Moretti (Assignee): Implemented initial CSS tokens; opened PR and flagged for visual testing. Need design decision on whether cancel button is visually inline or a collapsible affordance in toolbars. Suggest inline small-text 'Cancel' for touch and icon-only X for mouse/compact.

2026-02-02 - Ava Chen (Creator): Decision — use inline small-text 'Cancel' when there's enough horizontal space; otherwise render an accessible icon '×' with aria-label 'cancel'. Engineers to implement breakpoint logic based on container query if available, else size prop.
